data.name: Sample - Fortinet FortiAIGate - 1.6.0
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "Fortinet FortiAIGate" connector. If you are planning to use the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

workflows.name: Heal Expired FortiAIGate Key in Vault
workflows.description:
Keeps an application's FortiAIGate virtual key working. Reads the key from a HashiCorp Vault KV v2 secret and tests it against the data plane. If it no longer works, the playbook renews the same key - an expired key is extended (FortiAIGate only rotates an active key) and then rotated - writes the new secret into the same Vault path as a new version, and checks that the new secret works. The key keeps its id, name, limits, policies and model access; every other field of the secret is kept. A key that still works is left alone, and a revoked or suspended key stops the run with a message.
Inputs: secret_path (the KV v2 path, for example lab/ai) and, when the key is not stored under api_key, key_field. Outputs: rotation_result (a one-line outcome), rotated (true or false), key_id and key_method (rotated or extended_and_rotated). Run it from a schedule, or call it as a child playbook once per secret.

arguments.rotation_outcome: failed - new secret rejected by the data plane

arguments.rotation_result: {{ vars.rotation_outcome | default("renewed - new secret stored in Vault and verified") }}

groups.name: Note: ResolvePath
groups.description: The Vault path of the secret holding the key, and the field it is stored in. Read from the playbook parameters (manual run, schedule, child call) or, for an API trigger that sends them as top-level variables, from vars.

groups.name: Note: KeyValid
groups.description: Branch on the data-plane verdict for the stored key.

groups.name: Note: RenewKey
groups.description: Same key, new secret. FortiAIGate only rotates an active key, so an expired one is extended first.

groups.name: Note: BuildPayload
groups.description: KV v2 writes create a new version and drop omitted fields, so the new secret data is the whole current secret with only the key field replaced. Built as a JSON string because connector params are strings.

groups.name: Note: NewKeyValid
groups.description: The new secret must validate; anything else fails the run.

groups.name: Note: FailRotation
groups.description: Reachable only when the new secret does not validate.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Wizard-editable defaults. `range` is the backfill window used while the
watermark is missing or '0'. The macro name is scoped to this playbook's UUID,
so two ingestion configurations never share a watermark.

groups.name: Note: Environment Setup
groups.description:
Runs when the watermark macro does not exist yet, not only on the wizard's
`vars.request.env_setup` first pass. It must come AFTER Get Macro Value so its
absence can be seen: Update Last Pull Time only updates the macro, it does not
create it, so a missing macro would otherwise leave the watermark unwritten and
every run would read the backfill window again without any error.
The macro is primed to '0', which Set Time Configuration reads as a cold start.

groups.name: Note: Set Time Configuration
groups.description:
`curr_timestamp` is the end of this run's window, 60 seconds behind the clock
(see the block comment above). It is written back to the macro only after Ingest
succeeds, so a failed run reads its window again. `last_pull_time` is empty on a
cold start (macro missing, or '0'): the run then reads `range` instead, and
`until` stays empty because a custom window needs a start.

groups.name: Note: Save Result
groups.description:
The Fetch -> Ingest contract. Ingest reads every one of these back off the
workflow_reference step ("List Blocked Requests") as
`vars.steps.List_Blocked_Requests.<key>`.

routes.name: Create Record -> Update Last Pull Time

groups.name: Note: Mapping Preview
groups.description:
The Data Ingestion Wizard runs the Ingest playbook with
`vars.request.env_setup == true` while the analyst designs the field mapping in
the UI. In that mode the first fetched record is returned so the wizard can
render the Data Mapping preview; no alerts are written. `false` (or missing)
is the real ingestion path.

groups.name: Note: Return Sample
groups.description:
The sample for the wizard's Data Mapping preview: the first blocked request of
the window, whose keys are the fields `Create Record` maps. Falls back to a
representative record when the window is empty, so the preview still renders.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
The values the alerts take from the connector's output: the window's records
and the macro that holds its watermark. The severity is fixed in Create Record.

groups.name: Note: Create Record
groups.description:
The step is named "Create Record" because the Data Ingestion Wizard's Data
Mapping page is shown only for a create playbook with a step of exactly that
name, and it reads the target module off this step.

`is_upsert` routes this at /api/3/upsert/alerts, keyed on sourceId (the blocked
request's uuid), so a window read twice updates its alerts. Without it the plain
insert path 409s on the sourceId uniqueness constraint.

Only the alert fields below are set. Everything the gateway recorded is kept as
JSON in sourcedata (sourcedata must stay `| toJSON`: a bare {{ }} on a dict is
stored as the literal string "Array").

groups.name: Note: Update Last Pull Time
groups.description:
Advances the watermark only after the alerts are written, so a failed Create
Record leaves the window to be read again.
